Soft graviton theorem

Words: 83 Articles: 1
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The soft graviton theorem factorizes an amplitude with one low-energy graviton into the hard amplitude times a universal sum over external momenta. Gauge invariance of the soft factor requires energy-momentum conservation and universal gravitational coupling.

Weinberg soft theorem

Words: 48
Soft graviton theorem OurBigBook.com
The Weinberg soft theorem constrains interactions of a massless particle by requiring its soft-emission amplitude to be invariant under shifts of an unphysical polarization. For helicity one it gives charge conservation, for helicity two it gives universal gravitational coupling, and for higher helicity it obstructs generic long-range interactions.

Effective field theory (EFT)

Words: 387 Articles: 12
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
An effective field theory describes phenomena below a chosen energy scale by retaining the relevant light fields and organizing local interactions by increasing suppression at that scale.

Local operator (physics)

Words: 37
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A local field operator is built from fields and finitely many of their derivatives at one spacetime point. Its integral can deform an action, with the operator's scaling dimension determining the engineering dimension of the associated coupling.

Heavy-field decoupling

Words: 32
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
Heavy-field decoupling says that a field of mass M affects processes with external momenta p≪M through renormalizations of existing low-energy couplings and local higher-dimensional operators suppressed by powers of p/M.

Ultraviolet cutoff (Λ)

Words: 24
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
An ultraviolet cutoff removes modes above a chosen energy or momentum scale. An effective field theory encodes the influence of those omitted short-distance modes in its couplings.

Infrared divergence

Words: 16
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
An infrared divergence is a divergence caused by contributions from arbitrarily low energies or long wavelengths.

Quadratic Lagrangian

Words: 42 Articles: 1
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A quadratic Lagrangian contains terms of second order in field fluctuations and determines their linearized propagators and dispersion relations.

Higgs mode

Words: 23
Quadratic Lagrangian OurBigBook.com
A Higgs mode is a fluctuation in the magnitude of a complex or multicomponent order parameter, as distinct from a phase or orientational fluctuation.

Integrating out a field

Words: 41
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
Integrating out a field means performing its path integral while retaining the other fields as backgrounds. The result is generally a nonlocal quantum effective action; for a field much heavier than all external momenta, a derivative expansion turns it into local effective interactions.

Derivative expansion

Words: 36
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A derivative expansion expresses a nonlocal effective interaction as a series of local operators with successively more derivatives. For a field of mass M, each additional pair of derivatives is typically suppressed by M−2.

Four-fermion interaction

Words: 132 Articles: 3
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A four-fermion interaction is a local operator containing four fermion fields. In four spacetime dimensions it has mass dimension six, so its coefficient has mass dimension minus two; writing it as the square of a current multiplied by a coefficient inside the square gives that coefficient mass dimension minus one.

Fermi interaction

Words: 21
Four-fermion interaction OurBigBook.com
The Fermi interaction is the low-energy four-fermion approximation to the weak charged current. Integrating out a W boson gives its coefficient GF​/2​=g2/(8MW2​) at tree level.

Fierz rearrangement

Words: 38
Four-fermion interaction OurBigBook.com
A Fierz rearrangement rewrites a product of fermion bilinears with one spinor pairing as a sum of products with another pairing. For left-handed vector currents, it lets a charged-current four-fermion operator be compared directly with a neutral-current operator.

Fermi constant (GF​)

Words: 23
Four-fermion interaction OurBigBook.com
The Fermi constant is the coefficient conventionally used for the low-energy charged-current weak interaction. Tree-level exchange of a W boson gives GF​/2​=g2/(8MW2​).

Mass gap (Δ)

Words: 34
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum field theory has a mass gap when the vacuum energy is separated from the rest of the spectrum by a strictly positive energy. Correlation functions then typically decay exponentially at long distance.

Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB)

Words: 272 Articles: 7
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when the action and equations have a symmetry but a chosen ground state is invariant only under a proper subgroup. Acting with the broken symmetry generates a degenerate vacuum manifold.

Vacuum manifold

Words: 36
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
The vacuum manifold is the space of field configurations that minimize the energy. If a group G acts transitively and a chosen vacuum has stabilizer H, its connected component is the homogeneous space G/H.

Vacuum expectation value (⟨ϕ⟩)

Words: 39
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
A vacuum expectation value is the expectation of a field or operator in the vacuum state. A nonzero value that is not invariant under the full symmetry group can select a point of the vacuum manifold and spontaneously break the symmetry.

Scalar mass matrix (Mij2​=∂i​∂j​V)

Words: 35
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
The scalar mass matrix is the Hessian matrix of the scalar potential at a vacuum. Its eigenvalues are the tree-level squared masses; broken symmetry directions are zero eigenvectors before a Higgs mechanism or explicit symmetry breaking removes the corresponding massless modes.

Goldstone theorem

Words: 61 Articles: 1
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
In a relativistic quantum field theory, each spontaneously broken generator of a continuous internal symmetry produces a massless scalar excitation. For G→H, the standard setting therefore has dimG−dimH Goldstone bosons.

Pseudo-Goldstone boson

Words: 27
Goldstone theorem OurBigBook.com
A pseudo-Goldstone boson is a light mode produced when a spontaneously broken continuous symmetry is also weakly broken explicitly. Its mass vanishes with the explicit symmetry-breaking parameters.

Nonlinear sigma model

Words: 70 Articles: 1
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
A nonlinear sigma model has fields valued in a curved target space such as a vacuum manifold G/H. Its leading action is quadratic in spacetime derivatives but nonlinear in any unconstrained coordinates used for the target.

O(N) nonlinear sigma model

Words: 35
Nonlinear sigma model OurBigBook.com
The O(N) nonlinear sigma model has an N-component field constrained to a sphere, commonly n2=N or 1. An auxiliary Lagrange-multiplier field turns the constraint into a self-consistent mass gap in the Large-N expansion.

Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory

Words: 297 Articles: 11
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com

Z2 symmetry (Z2​ symmetry)

Words: 29
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A Z2 symmetry is generated by an operation whose square is the identity. For a real scalar field, the sign symmetry ϕ↦−ϕ forbids every odd power of ϕ.

Parity symmetry in quantum field theory

Words: 66 Articles: 2
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Parity symmetry means invariance under spatial reflection, together with the intrinsic transformation rules of the fields.

Parity-invariant vacuum

Words: 26
Parity symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A parity-invariant vacuum satisfies P∣0⟩=∣0⟩ up to an irrelevant phase. Vacuum correlation functions then transform according to the product of the intrinsic parities of their insertions.

Parity-odd scalar interaction

Words: 25
Parity symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A parity-odd scalar interaction is rotationally invariant but changes sign under spatial reflection. It must contain a pseudoscalar contraction, such as a Levi-Civita symbol contracted with three spatial gradients.

Charge conjugation (C)

Words: 52 Articles: 1
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Charge conjugation exchanges particles with antiparticles. For a matrix-valued gauge potential it acts as Aμ​↦−AμT​.

Furry's theorem

Words: 36
Charge conjugation OurBigBook.com
Furry's theorem states that a charge-conjugation-invariant vacuum has vanishing correlation functions containing an odd number of electromagnetic currents or photon fields. Consequently amplitudes with an odd number of external photons and no charged external state vanish.

Time-reversal symmetry (T)

Words: 13
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Time-reversal symmetry reverses the time coordinate and is represented antiunitarily in quantum theory.

CP violation

Words: 90 Articles: 2
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
CP violation is the failure of a theory to be invariant under the combination of charge conjugation and parity. Under CPT invariance it is equivalent to time-reversal violation.

Fermion electric dipole moment operator (ψˉ​σμνγ5ψFμν​)

Words: 37
CP violation OurBigBook.com
The fermion electric dipole moment operator couples a fermion pseudotensor bilinear to the electromagnetic field tensor. Its nonrelativistic interaction is proportional to S⋅E, so it is odd under parity and time reversal and signals CP violation.

CP-violating phase

Words: 25
CP violation OurBigBook.com
A CP-violating phase is a complex phase in couplings or mixing matrices that cannot be removed by field redefinitions and changes sign under CP conjugation.

CPT theorem

Words: 47
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The CPT theorem states that every local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory with a Hermitian Hamiltonian is invariant under the combined action of charge conjugation, parity and time reversal. An operator that is odd under CP must therefore also be odd under time reversal if CPT is preserved.

Standard Model (SM)

Words: 1k Articles: 53
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The Standard Model is a gauge theory with gauge group SU(3)c​×SU(2)L​×U(1)Y​. Its Higgs field breaks the electroweak subgroup to the electromagnetic U(1)Q​.

Strong interaction

Words: 19
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
The strong interaction is the SU(3)c​ gauge interaction described by Quantum chromodynamics. It couples quarks and gluons through color charge.

Weak interaction

Words: 150 Articles: 4
Standard Model OurBigBook.com
The weak interaction is the short-range chiral interaction mediated by the W and Z bosons. Above the electroweak scale it is part of the unbroken SU(2)L​×U(1)Y​ electroweak gauge theory.

Weak charged current

Words: 27
Weak interaction OurBigBook.com
The weak charged current couples a W boson to two members of a left-handed electroweak doublet. In the quark mass basis its flavor coefficients are entries of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix.

Weak neutral current

Words: 93 Articles: 2
Weak interaction OurBigBook.com
The weak neutral current couples the Z boson to a fermion without changing its electric charge. Its vector and axial-vector coefficients depend on weak isospin, electric charge, and the weak mixing angle.
Flavor-changing neutral current
Words: 63 Articles: 1
Weak neutral current OurBigBook.com
A flavor-changing neutral current changes fermion flavor without changing electric charge. Such currents are absent at tree level in the Standard Model and are strongly suppressed at loop level by the Glashow-Iliopoulos-Maiani mechanism.
Glashow-Iliopoulos-Maiani mechanism (GIM mechanism)
Words: 31
Flavor-changing neutral current OurBigBook.com
